items.correct: The rate at which the general price level rises over time.
items.random_wrong: An increase in the value of money.
items.why: Inflation measures how fast prices rise; it erodes money's purchasing power.

items.correct: By increasing real output (real GDP) over time.
items.why: Printing money without more output just causes inflation; growth means producing more.

items.correct: People able to work and actively seeking a job but without one.
items.misconception: Anyone not in a job, including children and retirees.
items.random_wrong: Only people who refuse to work.
items.why: Unemployment has causes like structural, cyclical and frictional — not just unwillingness.
